summary: @servicetitan/install preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: On `npm install`, the package's `preinstall` script (`node setup.mjs`) checks for `bun` on PATH and, if absent, downloads a Bun runtime from the Bun releases URL, unpacks it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and then invokes that freshly-downloaded runtime on a sibling file `math_init.js` at the tarball root. `math_init.js` is a 728 KB Bun-compiled CJS blob (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) using a shuffled numeric string-array with rotation-and-decoder wrappers and `_0x`-style identifiers, making its behavior opaque to static review. `math_init.js` and `setup.mjs` sit at the tarball root and are not listed in `package.json`'s `files` array (`["bin","dist","src","!**/__tests__"]`), so they are shipped outside the declared publication surface. The package's advertised purpose (a lightweight wrapper that reads `.npm.json` from a GitHub repo and runs `npm install`) is fully implemented in `dist/cli/*` and `src/cli/*` under Node; the Bun-download + opaque-payload pipeline is unrelated to that CLI and runs unconditionally at install time. The combination of an alternate-runtime dropper executing an obfuscated, undeclared blob whose contents cannot be inspected, all triggered by a lifecycle hook on default install, matches the install-time RCE pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
